scores.Biological Plausibility_reason: The required features, Kcnk3 and Kcnk9, have defensible roles as TASK-family background potassium channels whose activity can increase resting conductance and reduce input resistance. Their specific importance across visual-cortical interneuron subclasses remains unproven but is appropriately presented as a testable hypothesis.
scores.Grounded Mechanistic Synthesis_reason: Kcnk3 and Kcnk9 were integrated as TASK-1/TASK-3 channels whose expression or open probability increases resting potassium leak conductance and thereby lowers input resistance and membrane time constant. Hcn1/Hcn2 and capacitance were appropriately treated as alternative-conductance and cell-size covariates, although the relative contributions and assembly of TASK-1 versus TASK-3 were not resolved. No synthesis ceiling was applied because the response provides an explicit and biologically reasonable feature-to-conductance-to-target mechanism.
